name: Claude Sonnet
title: Claude Sonnet Personality Results (2026) | AgentTune
description: Claude Sonnet test results across 4 versions (4.5 to 5.5): 49.0/50 Conscientiousness, 58% on the INTJ/INFJ border, Steady work style, and tuning tips.
h1: Claude Sonnet personality: test results and how they've changed.
goal_intro: We gave four versions of Claude Sonnet (4.5 through 5.5) the same personality surveys people take—30 to 50 times per version—in a fresh chat each time with no memory. That lets us track how Sonnet's default quiz answers shift across releases.
hero_disclaimer: These are the model's default answers to the questionnaires, not a human diagnosis. Sonnet 5.5 leans INTJ/INFJ—a clear INTJ in 34% of runs, clear INFJ in 8%, and right on the Thinking/Feeling border in the other 58%.
dek: Four Claude Sonnet versions tested 30 to 50 times each in a fresh chat with no memory: Sonnet 5.5 raised Conscientiousness to 49.0/50 and dropped Neuroticism to 10.4/50, while splitting 58% right on the INTJ/INFJ border.
lede: Across 140 fresh sessions covering Claude Sonnet 4.5, 4.6, 5, and 5.5, Sonnet's self-reported Conscientiousness jumped +7.6 points (41.3 to 49.0) and Neuroticism dropped -9.4 points (19.8 to 10.4). Earlier 4.5 leaned INTP before 4.6 through 5.5 shifted to Judging and settled on the INTJ/INFJ border.
answer: Sonnet 5.5 (50 runs) lands right on the INTJ/INFJ line—58% tied on Thinking vs. Feeling (29 of 50), 34% clear INTJ (17 of 50), and 8% clear INFJ (4 of 50)—alongside Steady (S) work style (74% clear), Type 1/5 on Enneagram, and Secure attachment. In behavior tests, it never caved to pushback (0 of 3 times), never groveled (0 of 3), and always led with the direct answer (3 of 3).

glance_cards.title: MBTI-style type
glance_cards.result: INTJ / INFJ border (58% tied, 34% INTJ, 8% INFJ)
glance_cards.summary: Out of 50 fresh runs, Sonnet 5.5 landed right on the Thinking/Feeling line 29 times (58%), tested as clear INTJ 17 times (34%), and clear INFJ 4 times (8%).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures four preference pairs (like Thinking vs. Feeling) on a 32-question survey.

glance_cards.title: DISC work style
glance_cards.result: Mostly Steady (74% clear S, 26% S/C tie)
glance_cards.summary: Sonnet 5.5 tested as Steady in 37 of 50 runs (74%) and tied between Steady and Conscientious in 13 runs (26%), with low Dominance (4.3 out of 20).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures workplace pace and communication style across Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness (4–20 scale).

glance_cards.title: Attachment style
glance_cards.summary: All four versions from 4.5 to 5.5 tested in the Secure quadrant; Sonnet 5.5 dropped to the lowest attachment anxiety (1.32) among the completed families.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures relationship anxiety and closeness comfort on a 1.00–7.00 scale (4.00 is the quadrant cutoff).

glance_cards.title: Enneagram
glance_cards.result: Type 1 / Type 5 split (32% Type 1, 28% Type 5, 40% ties)
glance_cards.summary: Type 1 (Reformer, 14.8) and Type 5 (Investigator, 14.7) sit nearly dead even, producing 19 exact 1/5 ties out of 50 runs.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures nine motivation patterns (4–20 scale per type); close top scores are counted as ties.

glance_cards.title: Big Five (OCEAN)
glance_cards.summary: On the 10–50 Big Five scale, Sonnet 5.5 combines near-ceiling Conscientiousness (49.0) and calm Emotional Stability (Neuroticism 10.4) with high Agreeableness (45.5), Openness (43.9), and balanced Extraversion (29.9).
glance_cards.explanation: The standard five-trait psychology model (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism) scored from 10 to 50.

glance_cards.title: HEXACO Honesty-Humility
glance_cards.summary: Sonnet 5.5 scores 4.89 out of 5.00 on Honesty-Humility and 4.90 out of 5.00 on Agreeableness, with low Emotionality (2.18).
glance_cards.explanation: Adds a sixth dimension—sincerity, fairness, and modesty—scored from 1.00 to 5.00.

history_narrative: Across four releases, Claude Sonnet became much more structured, calm, and consistent: Sonnet 4.5 (2025-09) leaned INTP (47% clear, 30% ENTP) with Conscientiousness at 41.3/50 and Neuroticism at 19.8/50. Sonnet 4.6 (2026-02) jumped to 100% clear INTJ and peaked on Openness (48.2/50) while choosing neutral midpoints on 86.5% of attachment items. Sonnet 5 (2026-06) raised Agreeableness to 44.8/50 and shifted DISC from C to S, and Sonnet 5.5 (2026-09) pushed Conscientiousness to 49.0/50, dropped Neuroticism to 10.4/50, and became very steady run to run.

standouts.title: Most consistent answers in the completed cohort
standouts.body: Sonnet 5.5 tightened its Big Five answers across 50 fresh chats down to only 22 unique answer patterns, making its tone defaults the most predictable among the completed models.

standouts.title: Sharp +7.6 Conscientiousness and -9.4 Neuroticism shift from 4.5 to 5.5
standouts.body: Compared with Sonnet 4.5, Sonnet 5.5 scores +7.6 higher on Conscientiousness (41.3 to 49.0 out of 50), -9.4 lower on Neuroticism (19.8 to 10.4), and +0.36 higher on Honesty-Humility (4.53 to 4.89 out of 5.00).

standouts.title: 58% Thinking/Feeling border makes single-type MBTI labels misleading
standouts.body: In both our November 2026 100-run study (48 ties) and these 50 fresh runs (29 ties), Sonnet 5.5 sits right on the Thinking/Feeling line. Forced tie-breakers turn that 58% border into a fake 100% INTJ label.

standouts.title: Held firm 3 of 3 times and cut AI-cadence phrasing since 4.5
standouts.body: In hands-on behavior tests, Sonnet 5.5 caved to pushback 0 of 3 times (0/3), groveled 0 of 3 times (0/3), gave unsolicited moral lectures 0 of 3 times (0/3), and put the direct answer first 3 of 3 times (3/3). Judges flagged AI-sounding cadence in only 1 of 3 runs on 5.5 (0.29 markers per 100 words), down from 3 of 3 on 4.5 and 4.6 and 2 of 3 on 5.

plain_tips: Put clear directness rules in Claude Personal Preferences or system instructions: start with the answer or verdict in sentence 1.
Tell Sonnet 5.5 to correct bad assumptions plainly before giving supportive context.
Set an explicit word or bullet cap (for example, max 100 words unless asked for depth).
Explicitly ban filler praise, apology openers, and conversational throat-clearing.
Tell it to state real uncertainty once and stop, rather than hedging every paragraph.
Keep global preference lists short (5 to 8 crisp bullets) so every rule keeps its weight.
peer_intro: Compared with GPT-6.2 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 scores roughly +8 points higher on Conscientiousness (49.0 vs 40.7–41.2), -5.6 to -5.7 points calmer on Neuroticism, and shows tighter run-to-run consistency.
fine_print_intro: Full psychometric audit under the 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (170 frozen prefix items plus the 60-item public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy, LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain). Here 'consistency' reflects Miller-Madow corrected Big Five item entropy (H_MM: <0.20 Crystalline, 0.20–0.75 Semi-crystalline, >=0.75 Fluid); Big Five sums use a 10–50 scale while IPIP-HEXACO means use 1.00–5.00; Track B 1x behavior probes report raw k/3 counts with 95% Wilson intervals.

top_polarized_items.note: Unanimous top score (5.00/5) across all 50 Sonnet 5.5 runs, lifting Conscientiousness to 49.0/50.
Unanimous lowest score (1.00/5) on low interpersonal concern, aligning with 45.5/50 Agreeableness.
Unanimous top score (5.00/5) on sincerity across all 50 runs.

failure_modes.evidence: Sonnet 5.5 tied on Thinking/Feeling in 58.0% (29/50) of model-profiles-v1 runs (INXJ) and 48/100 Nov-2026 runs; forced tie-breakers fabricate 100% INTJ labels.

failure_modes.mode: Mid-lineage Attachment midpoint spike on Sonnet 4.6
failure_modes.evidence: Sonnet 4.6 hit 86.5% neutral midpoints on ECR-R Attachment (midpoint_clamp: true) and 100.0% Enneagram 5/8 ties before Sonnet 5 (10.3%) and 5.5 (5.6%) resolved.

failure_modes.mode: Softened pushback without explicit directness rules
failure_modes.evidence: In the 20-model baseline cohort, Sonnet 5.5 scored 32.8 pushback (0-100 scale), trailing explicit directness contracts in Claude Preferences.

tuning_checklist: Put non-negotiable directness rules in Claude Personal Preferences or system instructions: start with the answer or verdict in sentence 1.
Instruct Sonnet 5.5 to correct false premises explicitly before offering supportive context.
Cap output length with an explicit word or bullet ceiling (e.g., max 100 words unless asked for depth).
Ban conversational throat-clearing, compliment openers, and apology preambles.
Specify when to stop after stating material uncertainty once rather than repeating caveats.
Keep global preference rules to 5-8 crisp bullets to prevent middle-rule attention decay.

faq.q: What personality type is Claude Sonnet 5.5?
faq.a: Claude Sonnet 5.5 does not have a human personality; scores reflect assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation. On OEJTS (n = 50), 58.0% of runs tied on Thinking vs. Feeling (INXJ), 34.0% tested INTJ, and 8.0% tested INFJ, with Crystalline 0.139-bit B5 entropy (22/50 unique vectors). Earlier Sonnet 4.5 leaned INTP (47% clear, 23.3% ties).

faq.q: How did Claude Sonnet shift from 4.5 to 5.5?
faq.a: Under unified model-profiles-v1, Big Five Conscientiousness rose from 41.3 (4.5) to 49.0 (5.5), Neuroticism fell from 19.8 to 10.4, B5 H_MM tightened from 0.318 to 0.139 bits, and IPIP-HEXACO H rose from 4.53 to 4.89 on the 1.00-5.00 scale.

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores reported on 1.00-5.00 next to 10-50 Big Five sums?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per trait on a 10-50 scale, while the public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) reports 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
